主要内容: Procter & Gamble reported its Q4 2019 earnings, which exceeded expectations. The company's adjusted earnings per share reached $1.10, surpassing analyst forecasts of $1.05. Revenue also beat estimates, reaching $17.09 billion compared to the expected $16.86 billion. However, the company recorded a net loss of $5.24 billion, or $2.12 per share, due to an $8 billion write-down of its Gillette business. This one-time charge significantly impacted the financial results. Despite the loss, P&G shares rose 4%, as the earnings beat expectations when excluding the write-down. The company also provided an optimistic outlook for fiscal 2020. Organic sales increased by 7%, driven by price hikes and higher sales in developed regions. CEO David Taylor noted that this was the strongest quarter of organic sales in over a decade. The company is focusing on leveraging consumer data to accelerate product development and improve market shares. Procter & Gamble reported Q4 2019 earnings that exceeded expectations, with organic sales rising 10% in its health and beauty segment, which includes brands like Pepto-Bismol and Crest. The increase was partly driven by a late season surge in cough and colds, boosting sales for Vicks and ZzzQuil. The fabric and home-care segment, which includes laundry and dishwasher detergent brands, also saw organic sales growth of 10%. The company attributed this growth to its strategy of expanding the fabric-care market through higher-priced products like Tide Pods and Downy scented beads. P&G expects fiscal 2020 revenue growth between 3% and 4%, with a slight negative impact from foreign currency. Wall Street had forecasted revenue of $69.76 billion, up 3.5% from fiscal 2019. The CFO, Jon Moeller, noted that the guidance reflects a balance between market growth and competitive responses. The company also anticipates adjusted earnings per share to rise by 4% to 9%, with a modest net benefit from commodities, foreign currency, transportation, and tariffs.
